name: settings-tab-row
description: Settings tab row, an HTML rail. The rail (chrome/browser/resources/atrium/settings.js, renderSettings) is a <nav> of plain <button> elements with a click listener - there is no keydown handler at all, so the ARROW-KEY traversal this scenario originally proved (Pane.stepped(by:), a SwiftUI mechanism) has no equivalent here and can never fire. Measured directly: sending 'right' while General is focused leaves both captures byte-identical (delta=0.00) because nothing in settings.js reads the key. Rewritten to measure the thing that DOES move the selection on this surface - a click on the Appearance rail item - proving the selected-row fill still moves from General to Appearance the way the original scenario cared about, just via the surface's real input path. The rail is a 190px left column and `.selected` carries a background AND an accent text colour rather than a pill. A pixel coordinate and a pixel-region delta both die with a layout change. Rewritten to select the pane by element (`.settings-rail-item[data-pane="appearance"]`.click(), same pattern the-native-view-toggle-fades-in.json uses) and read the result back out of the DOM - the `.selected` class and the pane heading - rather than trusting a screen region to still be over the right pixels.

actions.note: let the browser window finish first paint
Atrium MUST be frontmost or cmd+comma opens Finder Settings instead - observed
open Settings; its menu item is not reachable from a scenario
window opens on General - renderSettings(root, PANES[0].id)
tab row, General selected - kept as evidence, not asserted on: a screen region over the rail is exactly what a layout move breaks

actions.expression: (() => { const b = document.querySelector('.settings-rail-item[data-pane="appearance"]'); if (!b) return 'no-pane'; b.click(); return 'clicked'; })()
actions.note: the Appearance item in the LEFT rail. settings.js has no keydown handler for the rail selection, so a click on '.settings-rail-item' is the only thing that moves it - same element-click pattern the-native-view-toggle-fades-in.json uses, chosen over a coordinate because this file has already paid once for trusting one across a rail move (see git history).
renderSettings() is a synchronous DOM rebuild, no CSS transition in settings.css - generous slack for the ssh/eval round trip, not an animation

actions.expression: (() => { const item = document.querySelector('.settings-rail-item[data-pane="appearance"]'); const heading = document.querySelector('.settings-heading'); return (item && item.classList.contains('selected') ? 'selected' : 'not-selected') + '|' + (heading ? heading.textContent : 'no-heading'); })()
actions.note: THE MEASUREMENT: proves the selection actually moved, both halves - the rail item's own '.selected' class and the pane that rendered in response - rather than inferring it from a screen region that has already gone stale once.
tab row, Appearance selected - kept as evidence alongside the eval above
